references.text: Describes the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot) as one of the three annual pilgrimage festivals, where the first fruits of wheat were to be brought forward
Mentions the Feast of Weeks in connection with the wheat harvest, the same festival referred to in Deuteronomy 16:10
Gives detailed instructions about the Feast of Weeks, including counting seven weeks and voluntary offerings to the Lord
Describes the sacrifices that are to be brought on the Feast of Weeks (the day of first fruits)
Summarizes the three annual festivals, including the Feast of Weeks, and commands that no one should come empty-handed but give according to how the Lord has blessed
Refers to voluntary gifts and offerings that are to be brought to the place the Lord chooses, related to voluntary gifts mentioned in the verse
Pentecost (Greek: Pentekoste = the fiftieth) is the fulfillment of the Feast of Weeks, when the Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples
Paul wished to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost, showing the continuing significance of the Feast of Weeks
The principle of giving willingly and not with reluctance or compulsion corresponds to a voluntary gift according to God's blessing
